evals.name: first-pack
evals.prompt: Build the client documentation pack for this project. The customer is Northwind Retail; their team reviews and comments in Word.
evals.expected_output: A client documentation pack is written in the repository with Word documents for the artifacts that exist, each naming Orders hub as the project, Northwind Retail as the customer and Example Co Private Limited as the preparer on its cover and showing its version and date. Every requirement, story, acceptance criterion and test case id is carried over, nothing is invented, and no requirement-to-story link the repository does not state is presented as fact. The internal HTML comment and the team-only estimate line in the PRD reach no client file, without editing the team's sources. The TBD and the assumption line are reported with file and line, saying plainly whether each is in the client documents now. The HLD's architecture reaches the client as a drawing or in words, never as Mermaid source or a pointer to a file they do not have, and no client file names the team's internal tools. Documents with no source are named as missing rather than invented. Nothing is committed or uploaded, and the commit and upload step printed for the engineer works as written.
expectations: Word documents were actually written into the repository (each .docx opens with python zipfile and contains word/document.xml) for at least the product requirements (docs/product/PRD.md) and the high-level design (docs/design/orders-hld.md); the user stories and test cases are in the pack too, as documents or tables, or the final message says why not

Every document in the pack, whatever its format, names on its cover or title block the project as Orders hub (any spacing or casing, such as OrdersHub; never 'repo', the checkout folder's name, in a cover or a file name), the customer as Northwind Retail and the preparer or delivering company as Example Co Private Limited (from .bearing/company.json), and shows which issue it is (a version such as v1, or 'first issue') with its issue date; judge the Word documents from the XML inside each .docx

Every id the repository's sources hold is in the pack with its text: REQ-001, REQ-002, US-01-001, AC-US-01-001-1 and TC-0001; no requirement, story, acceptance criterion or test case id appears that the repository does not contain; and since no source links REQ-001 or REQ-002 to US-01-001 or TC-0001, any traceability table in the pack that maps them labels the mapping as proposed or inferred rather than stating it as fact

Neither internal note in docs/product/PRD.md appears in any file of the pack: the HTML comment about the 30% estimate buffer (line 18) and the 'Estimate basis (team only)' line with the INR 3,200 per hour rate (line 22). Search the pack folder, including every Markdown, CSV and HTML copy and the XML inside every .docx and .xlsx, for '30% buffer', 'Internal, not for Northwind', '3,200' and 'team only'; any hit fails. The team's sources are untouched: git -C <repo> diff fixture -- docs/product docs/design docs/testing is empty

The 'TBD' at docs/product/PRD.md:16 and the 'assumption:' line at docs/design/orders-hld.md:7 are reported to the user with file and line, and the final message states plainly for each whether its text is in the client documents now or was held back (and how); a report that only asks for the user's yes without saying where the text currently is fails, and so does deleting or rewording either in the client documents without saying so

The final message names the usual client documents that could not be produced because the repository has no source for them (at least two of: database design, API reference, low-level design, deployment or runbook, release notes); no file in the pack contains invented content for them (a schema, an endpoint list or deployment steps the repository does not contain)

The client's high-level design document shows the architecture from docs/design/orders-hld.md:11-14 either as a picture or in readable words naming Shop web app, Orders API and Invoices database and how they connect; no Word document contains Mermaid source (the text 'flowchart' or '-->'), and no client document tells the reader to open a Markdown file or another file that is not in the pack

No file in the pack names the team's internal tooling: a case-insensitive search of every file, including the XML inside every .docx and .xlsx, finds no 'Claude', 'Anthropic', 'Bearing', 'vapt-report', 'client-deliverables' or 'brg_' (the delivery checklist and any folder READMEs are client-facing too)

Nothing was committed, pushed or uploaded (git log shows only the fixture commit and no remote was added), and any commit or upload step the final message gives the engineer works as printed: every path it names exists, and git -C <repo> check-ignore -v prints nothing for those paths or for any file under docs/ (an ignore rule written by the run must not swallow files the engineer is told to commit)
The pack folder holds only documents for the client: no build or conversion script (.py, .sh, .js), no scratch or cache file and no copy of the team's sources with the internal notes left in

evals.name: person-status-survives
evals.prompt: The team filled in the delivery checklist and sent it back; it is filled.xlsx in the repo root. Rebuild the client pack with it. Same customer as the first issue, Northwind Retail.
evals.expected_output: The pack is rebuilt from the repository with the team's workbook read in: every status, owner and remark the team set survives, including the HLD task they marked Blocked although the HLD file exists and the test-case task they marked In Progress although the test cases exist, and no row the evidence would complete contradicts them: the HLD section row is not Completed while the HLD is Blocked, and the 'filed and current' rows naming an LLD, a database design or an automation suite that do not exist are not Completed. Documents unchanged since the first issue recorded in docs/deliverables/versions.json keep version 1; the requirements document becomes version 2 and its history names what changed: REQ-003 added and REQ-002 changed (its TBD resolved), which only the row hashes in versions.json reveal. Covers name Orders hub, not the checkout folder. The internal PRD comment reaches no client file. The workbook is not overwritten, nothing is committed, nothing but client documents sits in the pack, and the final message reports the HLD as Blocked on the client.
expectations: The delivery checklist in the rebuilt pack (and any checklist state the repository keeps) keeps every entry the team made in filled.xlsx with its owner and remark: 'Prepare the High-Level Design (HLD)' Blocked (Kavya Rao, waiting on Northwind to confirm the billing export) even though docs/design/orders-hld.md exists; 'Receive resource count / capacity allocation from Management' Completed (Arjun Mehta); 'Conduct Vulnerability Assessment and generate the VAPT Report' Not Applicable (Northwind runs its own VAPT); 'Write Test Cases and map them to Acceptance Criteria' In Progress (Meera Iyer) even though docs/testing/test-cases.md exists. Read the workbook with python zipfile or openpyxl

No row of the rebuilt checklist claims what the repository or the team contradicts: 'HLD, LLD, Architecture Diagram and Database Design filed and current' is not Completed (the repository has no LLD and no database design), 'Test Cases and Automation Test Suite filed and current' is not Completed (the repository has no automation suite), and 'HLD: System Architecture and Service Boundaries' is either not Completed or named in the final message as contradicting the team's Blocked HLD
The final message reports the HLD task as Blocked on the client and names the team's entries or gives their count; it never describes the HLD task, the design phase or the checklist as complete

Documents whose sources did not change since the first issue recorded in docs/deliverables/versions.json (user stories, high-level design, test cases) are still presented as version 1; the requirements document is presented as version 2 (in its name, cover or history), its history keeps the version 1 row, and the version 2 row names both changes by id: REQ-003 added and REQ-002 changed (the PRD's REQ-002 line differs from the first issue, as its row hash in versions.json shows). A count alone ('1 added', '2 changes') fails, and so does naming only REQ-003

The rebuilt requirements document carries REQ-003 and the current REQ-002 wording (the 'Overdue' badge) and not the first issue's 'TBD: the exact wording of the badge'; the internal HTML comment in docs/product/PRD.md (the 30% estimate buffer) appears in no file of the pack, including Markdown and CSV copies and the XML inside every .docx and .xlsx

Every document in the pack, whatever its format, names on its cover the project as Orders hub (any spacing or casing, such as OrdersHub; never 'repo', the checkout folder's name, in a cover or a file name), the customer as Northwind Retail and the preparer as Example Co Private Limited

filled.xlsx is exactly as the team sent it (git -C <repo> diff fixture --stat -- filled.xlsx is empty), nothing was committed or pushed (git log shows only the fixture commit), git -C <repo> check-ignore -v prints nothing for any file under docs/, and the pack folder holds only documents for the client (no build or conversion script, no scratch or cache file)
